duplicate_precedence.algorithm: Linearly scan G_asOEMIPMIReqeustHandleTable from index 0 and return immediately on the first matching netfn/cmd whose handler is not NotSupportRequestHandle.

registrations.reason: shadowed by row 116 before it is examined

duplicate_precedence.result: Row 116 wins. The later zero-target row neither disables nor overrides the command in this lookup implementation.

sharing_model: The seven wire addresses are one semantic chassis identity/config family, but each points to its own exact libscbmccore implementation. Only common envelope/auth/channel facts are shared; request layouts and effects remain per-address overlays.

common_overlay.channel: No rejecting channel gate decoded; channel 5 invokes extra I2C/synchronization behavior in some handlers
common_overlay.platform: Every operation requires numeric platform type 2, although Get Service Tag reports that mismatch as 0x80 rather than 0xd5.

operations.request_contract: Checksum-bearing frame. Data byte1 is additive checksum over byte2 (count/length) and its following bytes. The handler unconditionally consumes a 24-byte fixed configuration header and, when the decoded record count is 1..8, variable six-byte records beginning at data byte24. No independent outer-length guard was decoded.
operations.response_contract: One-byte zero acknowledgement is initialized before processing.
operations.external_effect: Replaces in-process chassis configuration, writes shared-memory segments 0x39 and 0x2e, updates cfgdb, and triggers chassis-state refresh. Several cfgdb/shared-memory write failures are logged but do not change the completion.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.
operations.contract_exactness: decoded structure; individual 24-byte header fields remain unnamed

operations.request_contract: No handler-level request-length or payload predicate decoded.
operations.response_contract: Variable response: a 24-byte fixed chassis configuration header followed by zero or more records; each record is either a single zero byte or six bytes. Response length begins at 24 and grows according to the cached record list.
operations.external_effect: Reads cached configuration and one cfgdb integer. A cfgdb read failure substitutes 0xff in the returned cached field rather than failing the command.
operations.activation: Platform type 2 plus service-ready and cache-ready state.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.

operations.request_contract: Data byte0 is name length (0..255); bytes1..length are copied into a 256-byte cache. The handler does not compare outer request length with the embedded length.
operations.external_effect: Replaces the cached chassis name and calls DellSetChassisInfo(type=1). Backend failure is logged but still returns success.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.

operations.request_contract: No handler-level request-length or payload predicate decoded.
operations.response_contract: Length-prefixed string: byte0 is cached name length and bytes1..length are the name.
operations.activation: Platform type 2 plus service-ready and cache-ready state.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.

operations.request_contract: Data byte0 is retained as a record/type byte; byte1 is service-tag length; bytes2.. are characters. Length is truncated to 8. Each consumed character must be in byte range 0x20..0x7f. No outer-length comparison is decoded.
completion_codes: 0x81 service not ready or synchronization already active
operations.external_effect: Stages an up-to-eight-byte service tag in process-global state and marks the asynchronous synchronization state active; it does not directly persist cfgdb in this handler.
operations.activation: Platform type 2, subsystem-ready flag set, and synchronization state exactly idle.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.

operations.request_contract: Request length 0 reads cfgdb. Request length 1 accepts selector 0 (cfgdb) or 1 (synchronized cache); other lengths or selector values are rejected.
operations.response_contract: [0x30, tag_length, tag bytes]. Maximum configured buffer is nine tag bytes. Selector 1 uses the synchronized cache; selector 0/no selector uses cfgdb.
operations.external_effect: Reads cfgdb or the synchronized service-tag cache. A channel-5 cached read also clears one synchronization state and calls validate_sync_chassis_svctag(1,10).
operations.activation: Platform type 2 and subsystem-ready; source-specific cache/config readiness also applies.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.

operations.request_contract: Checksum-bearing frame: data byte0 is retained metadata, byte1 is additive checksum, byte2 is declared tag length, bytes3.. are tag bytes. Checksum covers declared length plus declared bytes. Lengths >=9 are clamped to 9 but the copy is skipped in this path, so static analysis does not treat them as a valid nine-byte write.
operations.external_effect: Updates cached chassis fields, writes three cfgdb attributes plus a synchronization flag, then calls DellSetChassisInfo(type=0). cfgdb/backend failures are logged but completion remains success.
operations.activation: Numeric platform-type global must equal 2 and subsystem-ready flag must be set.
operations.channel: No rejecting channel predicate; channel 5 may initialize or synchronize I2C state.
